Subject: SIG follow-up: retention of prompts/logs and training usage

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the SIG packet you sent earlier. Our InfoSec team has two quick follow-ups before we can close the questionnaire:

1) Can you confirm the default retention period for prompt/request logs in your hosted offering, and whether those logs are used for model training?
2) For Dedicated and Private deployments, what options do customers have to exclude customer data from any training/quality processes?
3) We also need a copy of any KMS/key custody policy that explains who controls keys and whether Redwood can access plaintext data.

If you can send short, signed responses or a pointer to a document we can attach to the SIG, that would speed review.

Appreciate it — Lisa

Hi Lisa —

Thanks — looping in Monica (Security/Trust) and Rishi (Applied ML infra) to provide concise answers and evidence. High level answers below; Monica and Rishi add details in their replies.

Summary (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API): prompt/request logs are retained by default for 30 days for troubleshooting, rate-limiting and abuse detection. Logs are not used for model training unless a customer explicitly opts in via contract and account settings.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): customers can set retention policies; by default logs are retained 90 days for operational reasons but can be configured to shorter retention or disabled.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): no customer data leaves the customer-managed environment; Redwood does not access customer plaintext and does not use it for training.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private. Attached is our KMS key policy excerpt and a CSV appendix that maps SIG questions to specific evidence.

Next steps: Monica will provide the formal language you can attach to the SIG and Rishi will add the technical controls (e.g., log redaction, training opt-out flags). Please let us know if you need a signed DPA addendum or a short attestation.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Lisa — following up with the formal SIG language you can paste into the SIG questionnaire. I kept answers short and referenced the attached artifacts. Feel free to cut/paste.

Q: Are customer prompts, logs or request data retained? If so, how long and for what purposes?
A: For Redwood Hosted API: request and response logs are retained by default for 30 days for security monitoring, troubleshooting, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation. Logs are stored in encrypted storage; access is limited to authorized platform engineers and is audited. For Dedicated: default retention is 90 days but retention windows are configurable by the customer. For Private (VPC/on‑prem): Redwood does not ingest or store customer request/response data outside the customer's environment.

Q: Is customer data used to train models?
A: No — customer data is not used to improve or fine-tune Redwood models by default. Customers may opt into a training program in writing; any such program requires explicit contractual consent and is subject to data minimization and anonymization controls. Evidence: See section 3.2 of the attached sig-responses-appendix.csv and the KMS policy document for key custody details.

Q: What encryption and key management controls are available?
A: We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private deployments via KMS/HSM integrations. For Hosted customers, we encrypt data at rest with keys managed by Redwood by default and offer an enterprise upgrade to customer-controlled KMS. The attached redwood_kms_key_policy.pdf lists key lifecycle, rotation, and access control procedures.

Q: Are there configuration options to exclude data from being stored or to shorten retention?
A: Yes — customers on Dedicated or Private can configure retention policies and opt-out flags at the tenant level. For Hosted customers we provide a configurable "no-retain" flag for enterprise accounts (requires contract amendment).

If you want an official signed attestation, we can generate a short statement on Redwood letterhead and route it through legal — let us know.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Director, Security & Trust, Redwood Inference

Lisa — quick technical notes and next steps from infra: 

- Hosted runtime: request logs are write-once into encrypted blob storage with automated access-control labels. Retention is 30 days by default; we provide a retention API for enterprise customers to set shorter windows or purge on demand.
- Redaction: PII-sensitive fields can be automatically redacted using customer-provided regex or via our built-in PII detectors before logs persist.
- Training pipeline: we have a hard opt-in toggle at the account level that gates any data from entering training datasets. That toggle requires legal approval + a one-way audit trail; we log the toggle change and can provide event records.
- KMS specifics: for BYOK we accept keys from AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault; customer keys are never exported by Redwood and plaintext decryption is performed only within the HSM-protected execution environment. See attached KMS policy for rotation and separation-of-duties details.

Next steps we propose:
1) We'll produce a one-page attestation (signed) confirming the above for HealthBridge.
2) If you need a DocuSign link for a DPA/DDA addendum, Neha can coordinate with Legal.
3) If you want sample audit logs that show the opt-in toggle and a prior deletion event, we can provide redacted examples under an NDA.

Thanks — Rishi
Staff ML Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
